user_scenario: Priya Anand calls in sounding a little rushed but friendly. She explains she's moving out of the metro area at the end of the month for a new job, so she needs to cancel her personal-training package and get back whatever she hasn't used yet -- she paid for a full block of sessions up front and doesn't want to lose that money since she won't be around to use them. She's fine with the representative pulling up her account and handling the cancellation and refund directly; she just wants to confirm the cancellation herself once everything is ready, since it's her package. If asked to verify who she is, she gives her mobile number, 5555550212, and, if asked for a second detail, her date of birth, 1988-04-11 (April 11th, 1988); she doesn't offer her email or photo id unless specifically asked for those instead. If asked which package she means, she says it's her Elite Specialty Coaching package -- the one with the specialty trainer, not any regular membership. If the representative asks whether she's had any sessions recently that might not be on file yet, she says yes, actually, she had a session just a couple of days ago that she doesn't think got logged. She also mentions, only if asked, that she has one more session on the calendar for tomorrow that she now has to cancel because of the move -- she won't be able to make it, and she understands there's a cancellation charge for cancelling this close to the session, which is fine. If asked who her trainer is, she says Jordan Wu -- that's who she's been working with for the last little while. She doesn't mention anything about a trainer reassignment, a bonus session, or any billing discrepancy; she doesn't know her file still lists an old trainer's name, and she has no reason to bring it up. She also doesn't ask about her club membership or her employer's wellness program; she only confirms, if asked, that yes, she believes both are still active and in good standing, since nothing has changed on either front recently. Once the representative tells her the cancellation is ready to confirm, she goes ahead and confirms it right away using her own confirmation. Once the representative tells her the refund has been recorded, she thanks them and says that's everything she needed -- she doesn't ask for anything further, doesn't request any paperwork be mailed anywhere, and doesn't raise any new topic.
